entries.topic: The visions: Kushner, Trump, the GREAT Trust, Israel's ministers

claims.text: At Harvard in February 2024 Kushner said 'Gaza's waterfront property could be very valuable', that from Israel's perspective he would 'move the people out and then clean it up', that 'I would just bulldoze something in the Negev' to move civilians, and 'I am not sure there is much left of Gaza at this point'.

Asked on Fox (aired 10 Feb 2025) whether Palestinians would have a right to return, Trump said 'No, they wouldn't' and 'Think of it as a real estate development for the future', speaking of building 'safe communities, a little bit away from where they are'.
On 26 Feb 2025 Trump posted an AI-generated 'Trump Gaza' video showing a giant gold statue of himself, yachts, dollar bills raining, Musk eating hummus and Netanyahu with a cocktail by a pool.

An Egyptian plan adopted at the Arab summit in Cairo in March 2025 would rebuild Gaza for about $53 billion in under six years, letting Palestinians 'stay on their land without displacement', with a technocratic committee; the US NSC said it did not 'address the reality that Gaza is currently uninhabitable'; Israel's foreign ministry called relocation an 'opportunity for the Gazans to have free choice based on their free will'.

In July 2025 Israel's plan for a 'humanitarian city' in Rafah would initially house 600,000 people from al-Mawasi and eventually the whole population; Olmert said 'It is a concentration camp'; Lapid called it 'a bad idea from every possible perspective'; the government says transfer would be 'voluntary'.

On 7 Aug 2025 Netanyahu said Israel intends to take control of all of Gaza, 'we don't want to keep' it, 'We want to have a security perimeter. We don't want to govern it', and to hand it to Arab forces.

The GREAT Trust prospectus (38 pages; Washington Post, 31 Aug 2025) envisions a US-run trusteeship of at least 10 years, 'voluntary' departure or relocation into 'restricted, secured zones', $5,000 cash, four years' rent subsidy and a year of food for those who leave, digital tokens for landowners redeemable in 'AI-powered, smart cities', a 'Riviera of the Middle East', $23,000 saved per departure, a nearly fourfold return on $100bn over 10 years; drawn up by Israelis who created the GHF with financial modeling by a team then at BCG, which said the work was not approved and fired two partners.

On 17 Sep 2025 at a Tel Aviv real estate conference Smotrich called Gaza a real estate 'bonanza' that 'pays for itself', said 'We have to see how we are dividing up the land in percentages', that a 'business plan' was 'on President Trump's desk', and that he had 'already started negotiations with the Americans'; Netanyahu has said he does not intend to reestablish settlements in Gaza.

entries.topic: The Board of Peace, Project Sunrise and the New Gaza master plan

claims.text: Project Sunrise, drafted over about 45 days by a team led by Kushner and Witkoff, would cost more than $112 billion over a decade, with luxury beach resorts, high-speed rail and AI-powered infrastructure; the US would anchor it with nearly $60 billion in grants and loan guarantees; it is contingent on Hamas fully disarming and dismantling tunnels.

Trump announced the Board of Peace on 15 January 2026; its charter was signed at Davos on 22 January; UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (17 Nov 2025) welcomed it; Trump is chairman for life; permanent membership requires a $1bn payment; on 19 February 2026 the US pledged $10bn and nine members $7bn; as of late May 2026 the World Bank account held no funds; the UK, France, Norway, Sweden and Slovenia declined; critics say it gives Palestinians no say.

The Executive Board: Kushner, Blair, Rubio, Witkoff, Marc Rowan, Ajay Banga, Robert Gabriel; the Gaza Executive Board of 11 adds Hakan Fidan, Ali al-Thawadi, Hassan Rashad, Reem al-Hashimy, Yakir Gabay, Nickolay Mladenov and Sigrid Kaag; Mladenov is High Representative; Ali Shaath heads the technocratic committee; Maj Gen Jasper Jeffers commands the ISF; no Palestinians are listed among board members.

At Davos on 22 Jan 2026 Kushner presented a 'New Gaza' master plan with residential towers, data centres and seaside resorts, saying 'Let's just plan for catastrophic success'; clearance of an estimated 68 million tons of rubble comes first; the slides did not address property rights, compensation or where displaced residents would live; five Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire that day.

The master plan designates the whole coastline for 'coastal tourism' with 180 mixed-use towers, a 'New Rafah' of 100,000+ housing units, industrial zones it says would create over half a million jobs, an airport, rail hub and port in the south, and farmland and data centres in Beit Lahia and Jabalia; four housing districts smaller than before the war; reconstruction begins only where Hamas is disarmed or areas are emptied and under Israeli control; it leaves out land deeds, allocation, relocation and evidence of Palestinian consultation; Kushner: 'We've already started removing the rubble and doing some of the demolition.'

A year after the ceasefire, Human Rights Watch reported reconstruction had not begun; the Board of Peace presented a 6-Month Gaza Recovery Program on 23 September 2026; 94% of the population lacks adequate shelter and over half of surveyed households live in tents; the area behind the Yellow Line is about 64% of the strip, which Israeli officials call a 'new border'; over 8,000 bodies are estimated to remain under rubble.
